claims.text: GDACS's tropical cyclone report for POLO-26 (GLIDE TC-2026-000184-MEX, reporting window 21-29 September 2026) records a Red alert (highest GDACS alert score) with maximum sustained winds reaching 287 km/h (Category 5) and an estimated 220 thousand people exposed to Category 1 or higher wind speeds in Mexico; the report notes 'Tropical Cyclone POLO-26 can have a high humanitarian impact based on the maximum sustained wind speed, exposed population and vulnerability.'

NOAA's National Hurricane Center Advisory Number 35 (200 AM MST, Tuesday, 29 September 2026) placed Hurricane Polo near 26.2N 111.9W, about 35 miles west-northwest of Loreto, Mexico, with maximum sustained winds near 80 mph (130 km/h) and higher gusts, moving toward the northeast near 10 mph (17 km/h) with significant acceleration expected as the center moved inland over Baja California Sur toward southern Sonora.

description: Hurricane Polo, a record-tying Category 5 eastern Pacific hurricane, made landfall on Baja California Sur just south of Las Barrancas at about 06:00 UTC on 29 September 2026 with sustained winds near 175 km/h before weakening further as it tracked toward Sonora. GDACS issued a Red alert for the storm, citing about 220,000 people exposed to Category 1-or-higher winds. NOAA's National Hurricane Center's Advisory 35 (2:00 AM MST, 29 September) placed the weakening system near Loreto with maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h (80 mph), moving northeast, with life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides possible across Baja California Sur and southern Sonora.

impact.summary: As of NOAA's Advisory 35 (2:00 AM MST, 29 September 2026), Polo had weakened to maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h (80 mph) near 26.2N 111.9W, about 35 miles west-northwest of Loreto, Mexico, moving northeast at 17 km/h after making landfall south of Las Barrancas, Baja California Sur, with winds near 175 km/h. GDACS's Red-alert report estimates about 220,000 people exposed to Category-1-or-higher winds. No confirmed death or displacement toll has yet been published by an authoritative source.

location.region: Baja California Sur and southern Sonora

event.scale: Peaked Category 5 (287 km/h); landfall as Category 3; GDACS Red alert

name: Hurricane Polo, Mexico

updates.text: Hurricane Polo made landfall south of Las Barrancas, Baja California Sur, around 06:00 UTC on 29 September with sustained winds near 175 km/h, then weakened further to 130 km/h (80 mph) by NOAA's Advisory 35 as it tracked northeast toward southern Sonora. GDACS holds the event at Red alert with about 220,000 people exposed to Category 1-or-higher winds.
